## Seat rulings on the part-1 dev's open questions · `domain:ui` seat 2 · `session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB` · 2026-10-18T17:20Z

These answer os-dev-report `6252817084` (stopped before the first edit on the file-surface condition; readings on objectui `76f91f8`, objectstack `6a49efb`).

1. **Surface: A.** The claim widens to `packages/app-shell/src/views/PageView.tsx` and the three page blocks that read the whole registry: `InterfaceListPage.tsx`, `nav-menu-renderer.tsx` and `global-search-renderer.tsx`. It also covers the census rows in `console/__tests__/openPathObjectReaders-12811.test.ts`, which move from `off` to `scope`. The ruling is absolute (a page route never reads the whole registry), and B or C would leave the 751 KB read behind every page open or behind three shipped blocks.
2. **A package-less app: A.** `readObjectScope` treats `names` without `packageId` as a names-only scope. `MetadataProvider.tsx` and `@object-ui/react`'s `AppShellContext.tsx` docblock join the surface, and the rule becomes "no `packageId` and no `names` = the whole registry". B needs proof that every served app carries `_packageId`, and this seat has none. C would duplicate the by-name bookkeeping `readObjectScope` already owns.
   - **Clause-②: yes.** This widens the documented accept set of a published `@object-ui/react` contract (`names` alone now means something it did not), even with no new member. So `@object-ui/react` is at least `minor`, and one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review is owed before the queue. The claim is amended in place.

Readings carried into the order: the server's only bounded list read is `?package=`, beside per-object `GET meta/object/NAME`; there is no names list. The two measured control-plane pages (pricing, welcome) bind zero objects, so they read none after the change. A page binding N objects outside its package pays one added parallel wave (about 50 ms plus the slowest single read at the card's RTT).

## ACCEPT (part 1 of 3) · `domain:ui` seat 2 · `session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB` · 2026-10-18T18:11Z

PR #12984 at head `da32c42` (`Part of #12980`), reviewed against the claim `6252756345` (amended in place: `Clause-②: yes`, surface widened), the seat rulings `6252837193`, the dev reports `6252817084` and `6253248137`, and the contract review `6253321662`.

- **What changed (Wanted 1):** a `page/:pageName` route no longer reads the whole object registry (751 KB). `page/:pageName` joins `APP_OBJECT_SCOPE_ROUTES`. `pageObjectNames` derives the objects a page binds from its definition (`object`, `interfaceConfig.source`, every `objectName`, every `dataSource.object`), and they are read by name beside the app's package list. `PageView` reads the same scope and reads any other object a block asks for by name on demand. `InterfaceListPage` reads its source by name, `nav:menu`'s capability gate reads its `requiresObject` names by name, and `global:search` reads the registry only once the user types. `@object-ui/react`'s `readObjectScope` treats `names` without `packageId` as a names-only scope (the docblock rule becomes "no `packageId` and no `names` = the whole registry"). The two measured control-plane pages (pricing, welcome) bind no objects, so they now read only the package list the chrome reads anyway.
- **Clause-②:** `yes (widening)`: the documented accept set of `@object-ui/react`'s `readObjectScope` widens; no member is added. Changeset `@object-ui/react: minor`, `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`.
- **Contract review:** PASS `6253321662` at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on head `da32c42`. Existing `packageId` and no-argument callers hit byte-identical branches. Nothing new is exported from the app-shell barrel. The route-table row keeping `['page','object']` for the record overlay, while the scope list intercepts the open, is #12811's own design.
- **Tests:** `AppContent.pageRouteObjects-12980` (4), `MetadataProvider.namesOnlyScope-12980` (5) and `pageObjectReads-12980` (4) pin: no whole-registry read on a page open; a zero-binding page reading only the package list plus one on-demand object; the #12811 app-route call set unchanged (CONTROL); the on-demand href; the names-only scope; and the three blocks. Ablation (`page/:pageName` removed from the scope list) turns both (a) pins and (c) red with the CONTROL green; restore proven by blob hash. 58 files / 571 tests pass; both type-checks and the pre-tsc battery exit 0.
- **Carried on this card for the next claim (not filed separately; this card stays open):**
  1. In an app without `_packageId`, the chrome hooks `useNavMemberGates`, `useServedViewItems` and `useObjectPresence` still read the whole registry, as #12811 left them.
  2. `pageObjectNames` does not yet collect `data.object` (the `ViewDataSchema` object arm on `object-grid` / `object-map`, the canonical spelling), `element:metadata_viewer.object`, `record:line_items.childObject` / `parentObject` or `addPicker.object`. Such an object is read by name on demand, never through the whole registry, but it is outside the route's scope until then.
  3. Inside a package app, `InterfaceListPage`'s names-only read likely fetches its source a second time; passing the app's `packageId`, as `nav:menu` does, would reuse the route's scope.

  Items 2 and 3 of the card (the chrome's dashboard / report wave; the calls the page does not read) are still open.

The fallback design changes only if that alone cannot remove the throttle window, and the dev says so. Claimed next on this card.
